checks.claim: Control rods absorb neutrons and slow down the chain reaction in a nuclear reactor.
checks.why: Control rods hold neutron absorbers (boron, cadmium, hafnium); inserted deeper they absorb more neutrons and slow or stop fission.

checks.claim: A nuclear plant's heat boils water into steam that spins a turbine connected to a generator.
checks.why: NRC and NEI: fission heat makes steam (directly in a boiling water reactor), the steam spins turbine blades and the shaft turns a generator; spent steam is condensed back to water.

sources.title: NRC: How does a nuclear power plant make electricity
NEI: How a nuclear reactor works

checks.claim: Cooling towers release heat as water vapor, and their white plume is not smoke.
checks.why: The visible plume is water vapor condensing into droplets as warm saturated air meets cooler air; it is not combustion smoke.

sources.title: Practical Engineering: Why are cooling towers shaped like that
IEEE Spectrum: steam from cooling towers

checks.claim: A thick concrete containment structure surrounds the reactor to keep radiation in.
checks.why: Containment buildings of thick reinforced concrete with a steel liner shield radiation and keep the reactor sealed.
